rules.law_name: California Civil Rights Council Criminal History Housing Regulations
rules.title: Limits on criminal-history screening in rental housing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use blanket bans against applicants with criminal records and may not consider arrests that did not result in convictions. Criminal-history screening must follow limits on what information is sought, how it is considered, and what action may be taken based on it.
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-record bans; no arrests-without-convictions policies

coverage.summary: Applies to California rental applicants when a landlord uses criminal-history information in tenant screening.

rules.exemptions: The document states landlords are not entirely prohibited from checking an applicant’s criminal history, but must comply with the limits.
rules.interaction: The document says the California regulations built on HUD guidance identifying criminal-history screening as a potential disparate-impact fair housing issue.
rules.quoted_span: The California regulations include limits on what type of criminal history may be sought, how an applicant’s criminal history can be considered, and what actions a landlord may take based on an applicant’s criminal history. Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.

rules.law_name: SB 329 Source of Income Amendments to FEHA
rules.title: Ban on refusing Section 8 or other housing subsidies
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to participate in government housing subsidy programs such as Section 8. A “No Section 8” policy is unlawful under the state fair housing source-of-income rules described in the document.
rules.key_value: Government housing subsidies count as source of income

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies when an applicant or renter uses a government housing subsidy program such as Section 8.
coverage.summary: Applies to California rental housing decisions involving applicants or renters using government housing subsidies.

rules.penalty: The document states the California Civil Rights Department is cracking down on violators and filed a lawsuit against a landlord that refused to accept Section 8 vouchers.
rules.interaction: The document states SB 329 amended the Fair Employment and Housing Act definition of source of income to include government housing subsidy programs.
rules.quoted_span: In 2019, the California Legislature adopted SB 329, which updated the definition of “source of income” used in the Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) to include government housing subsidy programs, such as Section 8.

rules.law_name: SB 267 Credit History Amendments to FEHA
rules.title: Credit-history alternative evidence for subsidized applicants
rules.requirement: A rental property owner may not use an applicant’s credit history in the application process when the applicant has a government rental subsidy such as Section 8 unless the owner offers the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their share of rent.
rules.key_value: Alternative evidence required before using credit history for subsidized applicants

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies when the applicant has a government rental subsidy such as Section 8.
coverage.summary: Applies to California rental applicants with a government rental subsidy when the owner uses credit history in screening.

rules.interaction: The document says SB 267 amended FEHA in addition to other recent state fair housing protections for renters using rental assistance programs.
rules.quoted_span: In addition, last year’s SB 267 amended FEHA to prohibit rental property owners from using a person’s credit history as part of the application process – if they have a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8 — without offering the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent.
